next_step: Finalize Dedicated commit tiers & burst proposal, legal review of SOC/KMS clauses, send redline to procurement
notes:
Lead: VP Product (Carlos M.). Mid-market B2B SaaS (product analytics) embedding LLM into in-app assistant + support workflows. Started with Hosted API PoC (Jan-Feb): good perf on small chat loads, spotted cost sensitivity at scale. Now evaluating Dedicated for predictable cost and isolation. Key asks: committed monthly GPU hours with predictable unit pricing, burst capacity for launch weeks, transparent overage rates, and a 3-month ramp schedule tied to usage thresholds. Security: must support SSO/SAML, SOC2 evidence, KMS/HSM integration, retention controls and a path for EU data residency later. Quote from PD: "We want predictable bills — sudden token spikes are a non-starter."  
POC summary: ran 2-week Hosted API trial for chat + doc search (approx 120k requests, 8M tokens). Observations: P95 latency on Hosted w/ 8k context = ~160ms for gen-lite model, cost avg $0.012/token-equivalent (too high for projected scale). POC success criteria: P95 < 150ms for interactive help flows, embedding recall > 88% on internal eval set, infra cost target ~ $60k/month at peak (after optimization).  
Pricing negotiation notes: AE proposed three-tier commit: 1) Base commit 2x reserved GPUs (monthly hours) for baseline traffic; 2) Burst pool + pay-for-burst at capped rate; 3) Overage = 1.5x committed unit price. Customer requests explicit ramp: month1 40% of commit, month2 70%, month3 full. Asking for a 6-month partial-credit runway if traffic under expectations. SE asked for quantization recommendations and estimated token throughput per GPU under their typical seq lengths.  
Procurement ask: include a SLA-backed latency target and a clause for fallback to hosted model variants if Dedicated capacity constrained. Legal wants KMS flow diagram + pen-test summary before signature. Roadblocks: internal procurement needs a 3-line TCO (monthly committed + expected burst + likely overage) and an ops runbook for incident handoff.  
Next demo scheduled 2026-03-18 (deep-dive on batching + cache settings). AE to deliver revised pricing deck with ramp schedule and an explicit example invoice (mock) by 3/16. SE follow-up: Sizing worksheet and CPU/GPU hour conversion by 3/14.
